blocks.content:
Governor can act without the advice of Council of Ministers in the following cases:
• Appointment of Chief Minister in a hung assembly
• Recommendation of President’s Rule (Article 356)
• Reservation of bills for President
• Sending reports to President

RRB frequently asks direct questions from this area.

items: Direct questions regarding Article 356 (Recommendation of President’s Rule) frequently appear in RRB exams.
Discretionary powers regarding a hung assembly and reservation of bills for the President are top competitive exam topics.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governor can act independently without the Council of Ministers' advice under specific discretionary scenarios.
Chief Minister appointment during a hung assembly is a key discretionary power.
The Governor has the authority to recommend President’s Rule under Article 356.
Reserving state bills and sending administrative reports to the President fall under discretionary duties.
